Team — drafting the CAIQ extract below (short answers, referencing attached evidence links). I started a shared Drive folder for MedSol: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_residency_pack

- Region residency (EU): Active inference nodes are present in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1. Typical active worker pool per region for dedicated private deployments: variable by commit; for Hosted/Dedicated we maintain a minimum active fleet of control-plane and worker instances for availability (we provide a dated snapshot).

- Tenant isolation: logical isolation via per-tenant deployment slices for Dedicated; for Private (VPC) customers, tenant compute is inside customer-managed VPCs or peered subnets — network ACLs and security groups enforce separation.

- KMS/HSM: We support customer-managed KMS keys (bring-your-key) and HSM-backed wrapping for key material; keys are partitioned per customer account and are never exported in plaintext. Refer to evidence document: redwood-kms-hsm-partition.pdf (in Drive).

- Logging/Retention (SOC 2 relevant controls): default retention for auth and admin audit logs = 90 days hot, archived to cold storage for 1 year. Longer retention options available via support request (enterprise packages).

I'll attach short blurbs for each relevant CAIQ control and mark the docs we can include in the packet. David — can you provide the peering diagram and the short runbook notes on where egress may occur?

- Marissa

From: David Kim <david_kim@redwoodinference.com>

Attached: vpc-peering-diagram-20270617.png

High-level peering notes: 
- For PrivateLink/VPC peering we terminate connections inside the customer VPC via interface endpoints. Traffic destined for inference compute in EU remains inside the peered path unless the customer routes traffic to an internet gateway intentionally.
- Potential egress points: (1) customer-controlled IGW, (2) explicit NAT gateway if configured, (3) cross-region replication for backups (we can control this with policy and note it explicitly in the packet).
- Failover/runbook: if primary EU node pool breaches capacity, routing falls back to a designated warm standby in the other EU region; we do not fail across into non-EU regions unless explicitly configured (policy default = restrict to EU).

I'll also attach a one-page runbook (privatelink-runbook-v1.docx) that lists connection checks, required SG rules, and an example traceroute to confirm private path.

-David

Katie — attaching the consolidated packet for MedSol (summary + artifacts). See attachments and short answers below. We included the drive pointer for full reference if your team needs deeper artifacts.

Attachments: redwood-residency-snapshot.pdf; privatelink-runbook-v1.docx; vpc-peering-diagram-20270617.png

Concise answers (for CAIQ reviewers):
- Residency: Active node presence confirmed in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1 as of 2027-06-17. Dated inventory included in redwood-residency-snapshot.pdf.
- Tenant isolation: Dedicated/private deployments run inside isolated network boundaries; per-tenant key partitioning for KMS; logical RBAC enforced via service-level tokens.
- KMS/HSM: Support for customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM-backed wrapping. We provide key partitioning per customer and documented key rotation practices.
- Logging/Retention: Default auth/admin logs retained 90 days hot, archived to cold storage for 12 months. We can extend retention under enterprise contract.
- Egress: Privatelink keeps traffic internal; egress only at customer-configurable points (IGW/NAT or explicit cross-region replication). Failover behavior is EU-only by default unless cross-region fallback is requested and agreed in writing.

If you want an annotated CAIQ extract mapping our answers to the specific control IDs, Marissa can add a one-page control matrix. Would you like that included in a follow-up?

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if you want to walk the reviewers through the packet.

Best,
